snippet.title: The Goal That Sent Two Countries to War | True Story
snippet.description:
El Clásico is a rivalry. Honduras vs El Salvador was a war. In June 1969, the two countries met in a World Cup qualifier: three matches, sleepless nights outside the team hotels, a burned flag, and a playoff in Mexico City guarded by 1,700 police. Less than three weeks after the final whistle, the armies crossed the border. The 100-hour "Football War" killed around 2,000 people. This is the craziest football story you've never heard.

If you love the biggest rivalries in football (El Clásico between Real Madrid and Barcelona, the Manchester derby, Boca vs River, Messi vs Ronaldo), this is the rivalry that went further than any of them. Long before the Champions League era and today's Premier League and La Liga superstars, two national teams played a World Cup qualifier that ended with fighter planes in the sky. A true football documentary about World Cup history, crazy football moments, fan riots, ultras and the darkest chapter in football history.

snippet.title: WHICH COUNTRY HAS THE MOST BALLON D'ORS?! | France, Argentina, Germany, Portugal, England, Brazil
snippet.description:
70 years of the Ballon d'Or, country by country: from Stanley Matthews in 1956 to Ousmane Dembélé in 2025, every Golden Ball counted for the winner's national team.

Argentina have 8, all of them won by one man, Lionel Messi. France also have 8, shared by six players: Raymond Kopa, Michel Platini (three in a row), Jean-Pierre Papin, Zinedine Zidane, Karim Benzema, and Dembélé, whose 2025 win drew France level at the top. Germany, the Netherlands, and Portugal follow with 7 each: Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Lothar Matthäus, and Matthias Sammer for Germany; Johan Cruyff and Marco van Basten with three each, plus Ruud Gullit, for the Netherlands; and Cristiano Ronaldo's five, plus Eusébio and Luís Figo, for Portugal. Brazil, Italy, and England have 5 each.

Tonight in London the tie can break: a win for Mbappé, Olise, or Dembélé would put France alone at the top, while Messi would give Argentina a ninth.

snippet.title: WHO WINS THE BALLON D’OR 2026?! | Yamal, Mbappé, Messi, Rodri, Kane, Haaland, Olise or Dembélé
snippet.description:
The ceremony takes place on 26 October in London, the first time in the award's 70-year history it is held outside France, and eight superstars are in the race: Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi, Rodri, Harry Kane, Erling Haaland, Michael Olise, and reigning winner Ousmane Dembélé.
  
Lamine Yamal won La Liga, the Spanish Super Cup, and the 2026 World Cup with Spain after a season of 26 goals and 21 assists, and could become the first player under 21 to lift the Golden Ball. His teammate Rodri, the 2024 winner, was named best player of the World Cup before his move to Barcelona. Lionel Messi is chasing a record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or after a remarkable World Cup at 39. Kylian Mbappé finished as top scorer in both the Champions League and La Liga with Real Madrid, Harry Kane and Michael Olise powered Bayern Munich, Erling Haaland kept scoring for Manchester City, and Dembélé led PSG to back-to-back Champions League titles.
  
There's even more at stake: Barcelona and Real Madrid are tied on 12 Ballon d'Ors each, so a win for Yamal, Rodri, or Mbappé would put their club alone at the top

snippet.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo has walked out of the Portugal national team camp, and reports say his international career may be over. On 27 September, the 41-year-old spent an entire national team match on the bench for the first time in 18 years, during Portugal's Nations League clash with Norway. Head coach Jorge Jesus then made it clear publicly that nobody would force him to change his tactical plans, even if it meant the veteran sitting out.

Ronaldo skipped training, left the team hotel in Copenhagen while his teammates were on the pitch, and posted a statement saying that after the coach's press conference and a conversation with Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença, he decided to leave the camp – promising to tell the Portuguese people the full truth behind his exit when the time is right. Portuguese outlet O Jogo reports that Ronaldo has made a final decision not to play for Portugal again, which would make the 1-0 win over Wales his last international appearance. The federation's disciplinary rules allow a ban of one to six months for leaving the camp without permission.

The timing is remarkable: Lionel Messi is preparing for an emotional farewell match with Argentina on 6 October, while football's all-time top scorer, closing in on 1,000 career goals with Al-Nassr, appears to be leaving his national team in a storm of controversy.
